text: The region of the stack holding one call's parameters, local variables, and return address is called a stack ___ .
explanation: Chapter 25 builds the same thing deliberately: `apply` creates a new `Env` per call rather than per procedure, which is why a recursive procedure has a different parameter value at each depth. A frame holds a call's locals; an `Env` holds a call's locals. The correspondence is exact, and noticing it is most of what writing an interpreter does to your understanding of the language you wrote it in.
